title: Unequal Exponents
statement: Positive real numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$ satisfy $a + b + c = 3$. Find the largest possible value of $ab^2c^3$. Give your answer as a fraction in lowest terms.
hints: Try to write $a + b + c$ as a sum of six terms whose product is a fixed multiple of $ab^2c^3$.
Apply AM-GM to the six numbers $a$, $\frac{b}{2}$, $\frac{b}{2}$, $\frac{c}{3}$, $\frac{c}{3}$, $\frac{c}{3}$, and find when equality holds.
solution:
The six numbers $a, \frac{b}{2}, \frac{b}{2}, \frac{c}{3}, \frac{c}{3}, \frac{c}{3}$ add up to $3$, so by AM-GM
$$\dfrac{ab^2c^3}{4 \cdot 27} \le \left(\dfrac{3}{6}\right)^6 = \dfrac{1}{64}.$$
Hence $ab^2c^3 \le \frac{108}{64} = \frac{27}{16}$, with equality when $a = \frac{b}{2} = \frac{c}{3} = \frac{1}{2}$, that is, at $(a, b, c) = (\frac{1}{2}, 1, \frac{3}{2})$. The largest value is $\frac{27}{16}$.
